name: Cytomegalovirus Disease in Patients with Impaired Cell-Mediated Immunity Deemed at Risk

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: CMV Disease Diagnostic Criteria in Immunocompromised Patients

criteria.description: Presence of clinical symptoms consistent with CMV end-organ disease (e.g., pneumonitis, colitis, retinitis)
Detection of CMV DNA by PCR or CMV antigenemia in blood or affected tissue
Histopathological evidence of CMV inclusion bodies or positive immunohistochemistry in tissue biopsy
Documented impaired cell-mediated immunity (e.g., transplant recipient, HIV infection with low CD4 count)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms consistent with CMV disease plus virological evidence of CMV infection in a patient with impaired cell-mediated immunity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is supportive but not mandatory if clinical and virological criteria are met.

laboratory: Positive CMV PCR in blood or tissue samples
imaging: Chest CT showing bilateral interstitial infiltrates in CMV pneumonitis
MRI brain abnormalities in CMV encephalitis
Fundoscopic examination revealing retinal hemorrhages and necrosis
genetic: No specific genetic markers; disease related to immunosuppression status
other: Histopathological identification of owl’s eye intranuclear inclusions in biopsy specimens

distinguishingFeatures: HSV lesions typically more localized and vesicular
HSV encephalitis has predilection for temporal lobes
EBV often causes lymphadenopathy and B-cell proliferation
Serology and PCR for EBV distinguish from CMV
Histopathology differs with presence of Reed-Sternberg-like cells

redFlags: Rapid onset of visual loss indicating CMV retinitis
Progressive respiratory failure in suspected CMV pneumonitis
Neurological deterioration suggestive of CMV encephalitis
references: Cannon MJ, Schmid DS, Hyde TB. Review of cytomegalovirus seroprevalence and demographic characteristics associated with infection. Rev Med Virol. 2010.
Kotton CN, et al. The Third International Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Cytomegalovirus in Solid-organ Transplantation. Transplantation. 2018.
Ljungman P, et al. Cytomegalovirus in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: Current Status, Challenges, and Future Directions. Clin Infect Dis. 2019.
